title: Add tracing context propagation + request-id capture helpers
author: Ibrahim Khan
release_notes: - Python SDK: new helpers for extracting/injecting W3C trace context and capturing x-redwood-request-id to simplify template instrumentation.
body:
Title: Add tracing context propagation + request-id capture helpers

Context
DevEx quickstart templates (RAG + agents) need to emit useful traces/logs with minimal boilerplate. Today, template code has to:
- manually plumb trace context into outbound tool/retriever calls
- locate and log Redwood request IDs from responses
- handle streaming responses consistently

This PR adds small, opt-in helpers in the Python SDK to standardize:
1) extracting inbound trace context from HTTP headers (W3C Trace Context + Baggage)
2) injecting active span context into outbound request headers
3) capturing x-redwood-request-id (and surfacing it in errors) so templates can correlate logs/traces with Redwood Console

What’s included
- redwood_sdk/telemetry/context.py
  - extract_context(headers) -> Context
    - uses opentelemetry.propagate (supports traceparent/tracestate + baggage)
    - accepts Mapping[str, str] and normalizes header casing
  - inject_context(headers: MutableMapping[str, str], context: Optional[Context] = None) -> None
    - injects current (or provided) context into headers
  - get_redwood_request_id(headers) -> Optional[str]
    - returns x-redwood-request-id if present (case-insensitive)
- redwood_sdk/_httpx.py
  - request/stream entrypoints now optionally capture request id from response headers and attach it to raised APIError (as request_id)
  - preserves current behavior if header missing
- redwood_sdk/errors.py
  - APIError now has optional request_id attribute (and includes it in __str__ when present)
- docs snippet update
  - minimal example showing how templates can bind request_id into structured logs without parsing raw headers

Usage examples
1) Inject trace context into outbound tool calls (template-side):

from redwood_sdk.telemetry.context import inject_context

headers = {"user-agent": "my-app"}
inject_context(headers)  # uses current span context
resp = httpx.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=...)

2) Extract incoming context in a web server (template-side):

from redwood_sdk.telemetry.context import extract_context
from opentelemetry import trace

ctx = extract_context(request.headers)
with trace.get_tracer(__name__).start_as_current_span("http.request", context=ctx):
    ...

3) Surface x-redwood-request-id for support/debug:

try:
    client.responses.create(...)
except APIError as e:
    logger.error("redwood request failed", extra={"redwood_request_id": e.request_id})
    raise

Notes / decisions
- We use OpenTelemetry propagators rather than implementing custom parsing. This keeps us aligned with internal standards and lets customers swap propagators if needed.
- We intentionally do not add any new automatic span creation in the SDK in this PR. Templates and apps remain in control of span boundaries; this change is about propagation + correlation.
- We treat request-id capture as best-effort and do not fail if headers are unavailable (e.g., network error before response).

Files changed (high level)
- redwood_sdk/telemetry/context.py (new)
- redwood_sdk/_httpx.py
- redwood_sdk/errors.py
- redwood_sdk/__init__.py (exports)
- tests/test_telemetry_context.py (new)
- tests/test_request_id_capture.py (new)
- docs/observability.md (snippet)

Illustrative snippet (errors.py)

class APIError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message: str, *, status_code: int | None = None, request_id: str | None = None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status_code = status_code
        self.request_id = request_id

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        base = super().__str__()
        if self.request_id:
            return f"{base} (redwood_request_id={self.request_id})"
        return base

Test plan
- unit tests covering:
  - case-insensitive request-id extraction
  - inject/extract round-trip using the global propagator
  - error includes request_id when response includes header
- manual:
  - ran template app with OTel collector locally; verified downstream tool calls carry traceparent
  - verified request_id appears in logs on a forced 401 and 429

Checklist
- [x] Backwards compatible (no signature changes required)
- [x] New helpers are opt-in
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Docs snippet updated

Review conversation (highlights)
- Monica Patel: “Can we keep the surface area tiny? Templates should call 1-2 helper funcs, not learn SDK internals.”
  - Ibrahim: kept helpers in redwood_sdk.telemetry.context with three functions; avoided httpx-specific types.
- Allison Grant: “Please ensure we don’t encourage high-cardinality attributes. Request-id is fine in logs, but don’t default to metric labels.”
  - Ibrahim: updated docs to recommend request-id for logs/traces only; no metrics examples.
- Brian Murphy: “Does x-redwood-request-id exist on streaming responses consistently?”
  - Ibrahim: yes for initial response headers; capture happens once on response open. Added a test using the streaming code path.
- Christine Wong: “Make sure we don’t leak auth headers when propagating.”
  - Ibrahim: inject_context only adds trace headers (traceparent/tracestate/baggage). No copying of inbound headers.

- python-lint: pass

Outcome
Merged (squash) after requested doc tweak and adding streaming-path coverage.
